overview: Lombard rule in Italy supported a distinctive synthesis of architecture, Christian patronage and inherited Roman knowledge. Northern kings and southern duchies require separate political histories.

items.text: Lombard monuments combined Roman, Byzantine and Germanic traditions in churches, monasteries and secular buildings.
Stucco, painted decoration and architectural sculpture formed part of surviving elite monuments.
Lombard institutions helped transmit ancient literary, legal, technical and historical works into medieval Europe.
Support for monasteries strengthened religious networks. The sanctuary of St Michael at Monte Sant'Angelo became an important pilgrimage destination.

sources.title: UNESCO: Longobards in Italy, Places of the Power
